Q: Can I create key binding for my snippet in Geany? A:

Using the [Keybindings] part in file snippets.conf.

Attention: These key bindings can be overridden by Geany's configurable key bindings, i.e., key bindings from menu Edit → Preferences → Keybindings.

In the case you want using this way to create a keyboard shortcut for a snippet, but it is already in the Geany's configurable key bindings, you need to change this keyboard shortcut in the Geany's configurable key bindings.

References

  • User-definable snippets, Snippet keybindings (Geany manual)

Q: Cannot find Cuda while compiling example-app using Libtorch c++ library A:

You're using CMake wrong. In a CMakeList.txt script, you do not - typically - tell CMake what the compiler is, what the platform is, where system libraries are etc. You tell it about your project, and declare the project's external dependencies. So, in your case:

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.26) # or some other min version
project(Example LANGUAGES CXX)
find_package(CUDAToolkit 12.1 REQUIRED)
add_executable(MLA src/main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(MLA PRIVATE CUDA::cudart CUDA::cuda_driver)

that's not the actual CMake script you would use, it's just a part of it without the Torch stuff. Also, I don't know which of the CUDA libraries you actually need, I chose two of the popular ones. The full list is in the documentation. I am also assuming there is proper CMake support in Torch, so that you can also find_package(Torch), and then maybe it will defined the CUDA dependencies itself and you won't even have to bother.

As for the compiler and platform info etc. - let CMake find them; or if you want to override them, invoke CMake with the appropriate defines (e.g. -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mycompiler), set environment variables, use toolchain files etc.
